segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they gave a dinner for him there. Martha was serving, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at the table with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Mary took a pound of very costly perfumed oil, pure nard, and anointed Jesus’s feet and wiped his feet with her hair, and the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfumed oil.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples, the one who was about to hand him over, said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why wasn’t this perfumed oil sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief; he kept the money box and used to take what was put into it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Leave her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of my burial.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A large crowd of the Jews learned that he was there, and they came, not only because of Jesus but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: because on account of him many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The next day the large crowd that had come to the festival heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They took palm branches and went out to meet him, shouting,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, as it is written:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Do not be afraid, daughter Zion. Look, your king is coming, seated on a donkey’s colt.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His disciples did not understand these things at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written about him and that they had done these things to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the crowd that had been with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept bearing witness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This was also why the crowd went to meet him: they had heard that he had done this sign.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Pharisees said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You see that you are getting nowhere. Look, the world has gone after him!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now among those who went up to worship at the festival were some Greeks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip went and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever loves their life loses it, and whoever hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone serves me, they must follow me, and where I am, there my servant will be also. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say? ‘Father, save me from this hour’? But it was for this that I came to this hour.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Father, glorify your name.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a voice came from heaven:

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The crowd standing there heard it and said it had thundered. Others said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “An angel has spoken to him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This voice has come not for my sake but for yours.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be thrown out.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said this to indicate the kind of death he was going to die.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the crowd answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We have heard from the Law that the Messiah remains forever. So how can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The light is among you a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you; whoever walks in the darkness does not know where they are going.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become children of light.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said these things, then went away and hid from them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Though he had done so many signs in front of them, they did not believe in him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah said again:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they would not see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Isaiah said these things because he saw his glory and spoke about him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nevertheless, many even among the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they did not acknowledge it, so that they would not be put out of the synagogue;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for they loved the glory that comes from people more than the glory that comes from God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus cried out and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever believes in me believes not in me but in the one who sent me,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have come into the world as light, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in the darkness.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge that person, for I did not come to judge the world but to save the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever rejects me and does not receive my words has a judge: the word that I have spoken will judge that person on the last day.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For I have not spoken on my own; the Father who sent me has himself given me a command, what to say and what to speak.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And I know that his command is eternal life. So the things I speak, I speak just as the Father has told me.”

notes.note: The Greek adjective is rare and its meaning is uncertain. Most scholars take it as “genuine” or “unadulterated”, which suits an expensive import that was often diluted; other proposals are “liquid” or a trade name for a kind of nard. Mark 14:3 uses the same phrase. The “pound” is the Roman pound, about 325 grams or twelve ounces.

The verb is the ordinary word for handing a person or thing over to someone else, and the Gospels use it of Jesus being handed over by Judas, by the chief priests and by Pilate alike. English tradition renders it “betray” when Judas is the subject, a fair inference from the story but narrower than the word itself. The standard lexicons give “hand over, deliver up” as its meaning.

notes.traditional: three hundred pence; a year’s wages
notes.note: A denarius was a Roman silver coin, roughly a day’s pay for a laborer. Three hundred denarii was therefore close to a year’s wages for a working man.

notes.traditional: bare what was put therein; used to help himself to what was put into it
notes.note: The verb means “carry” and can also mean “carry off”, that is, steal. The sentence could say only that Judas carried the common fund, but coming straight after “he was a thief” most scholars read it as pilfering, and the translation follows them.

notes.phrase: so that she may keep it for the day of my burial
notes.traditional: against the day of my burying hath she kept this
notes.note: The Greek is compressed and its sense is disputed. It may mean “let her keep it for the day of my burial”, or, with words supplied, “she did not sell it so that she could keep it for this”, with the anointing itself anticipating his burial. Later manuscripts smooth the difficulty to “she has kept it”. The word for burial refers to preparing a body for the tomb.

A Hebrew cry meaning “save, please”, from Psalm 118:25, the psalm the crowd goes on to quote. By the first century it was used as a shout of acclamation at festivals, so it is kept as the cry it was and not translated. Palm branches were associated with national celebration and victory.

The phrase is a biblical personification of Jerusalem itself as a young woman: Zion is the daughter, not her parent. “Daughter of Zion” is the familiar wording, but it suggests someone who belongs to Zion; several modern translations now use “daughter Zion”. The quotation is a shortened form of Zechariah 9:9.

notes.phrase: when he called Lazarus out of the tomb
notes.note: Some early manuscripts read “that” where others read “when”, a difference of one letter in Greek. With “that”, the verse says the crowd with him kept testifying that he had called Lazarus out of the tomb. The edition translated here reads “when”, which makes this crowd the eyewitnesses from Bethany, distinct from the festival crowd of verse 18.

The word here is the one for a person’s own life or self, the same word rendered “soul” in verse 27. It is a different Greek word from the “life” in “eternal life” at the end of the verse. “Hates” is a Semitic way of expressing sharp preference, putting one thing decisively second to another, and not a call to self-loathing.

In Jewish usage this phrase meant the life of the age to come, the new era God would bring in. It describes a kind of life as well as an unending length of it. “Eternal” is the standard rendering and is kept here; a minority of translators prefer “life of the age to come”.

notes.phrase: Father, save me from this hour
notes.note: Ancient manuscripts had no punctuation, so this can be read either as a prayer Jesus considers and sets aside (“Shall I say, ‘Father, save me’?”) or as a prayer he actually prays and then at once overrides. The edition translated here punctuates it as a statement; most English translations take it as a question, as this one does. On either reading the next sentence gives his decision.

The verb means both to raise something physically and to exalt or honor someone. John uses it with both senses at once: Jesus is raised up on the cross, as verse 33 explains, and that same event is his exaltation. The Greek conjunction is literally “if”, but it expresses no doubt about the event. Some manuscripts read “all things” in place of “all people”.

The Greek word translates the Hebrew for “anointed one” and here is a title for the king Israel expected, not a name for Jesus, so “Messiah” is used. Several modern translations make the same distinction in the Gospels. “The Law” here stands for the Scriptures generally; the crowd is probably thinking of promises that David’s line and kingdom would last forever.

The quotation in verse 40 comes from Isaiah 6, where the prophet sees the Lord enthroned in the temple. “His” and “him” here most naturally refer to Jesus: John is saying that the glory Isaiah saw was Christ’s. Some manuscripts read “when he saw” in place of “because he saw”.

candidates.reason: Rendered “betray” for Judas but “hand over/deliver” elsewhere in most translations; one decision is needed so the repeated verb stays visible across the passion narratives and Paul.
Translators vary between “life”, “soul” and “self”, and the choice bears on how readers hear sayings about losing and saving one’s life across the Gospels.
Jesus’s formula (doubled in John) is rendered “truly”, “verily”, “amen” or “very truly” in different translations and recurs throughout all four Gospels.
A fixed title across the Gospels where capitalization and wording (“Son of Man”, “the Human One”) need one policy.
Covers divine splendor and human reputation or praise (vv. 41, 43); translations split between “glory”, “praise” and “honor”, which hides John’s wordplay unless handled consistently.

warnings: Verse 11: πιστεύω is not rendered with a register form (believe / trust) and has no register-exception note.
